previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of two kidney transplants was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting one day, accompanied by low-grade fever and orthostatic hypotension. She reported sick contacts—her young son and husband—developing similar symptoms. Initial evaluation revealed volume depletion, but no signs of bacterial infection, C. difficile, or influenza. CMV viral load was not detected. She was managed with IV fluids, continued immunosuppressive therapy, and symptom control with Zofran. Her condition improved rapidly, with resolution of vomiting and fever, and she began tolerating oral intake. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all baseline medications, adjusted atenolol dose, and follow up on pending culture and viral load results.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with Type I DM, HTN, ESRD s/p living donor 
renal transplant in ___ presents with 5 days of low grade fever 
and non-productive cough.
.
# Fever and cough- history and exam most suggestive of viral 
bronchitis. No clear infiltrate on chest film to suggest 
bacterial pneumonia. Patient not hypoxic, and is compliant with 
Bactrim for PCP ___. No history of obstructive lung 
disease to suggest chronic bronchitis. Modified Wells score is 
zero. Influenza on differential, although lower suspicion given 
gradual onset of symptoms, recent vaccination, and late in the 
season. Completed five days of oseltamivir. Abnormal UA and 
history of fever with previous urinary tract infection as the 
etiology of the fever.  Was continued on benzonatate for cough 
suppression.  Albuterol for bronchospasms.  Viral cultures and 
legionella was negative.  Was discharged to complete five days 
of levaquin for presumed urinary tract infection even though the 
culture was negative (though on antibiotics)
